cases.attempt: A program whose outcome depends on data being described by printed appearance: PIC 9(3) DISPLAY occupying 3 character positions.
cases.reason: One sentence naming a concept ('The concept used in describing data ...'); the sizes a program can observe are required by the PICTURE and USAGE rows, not by this sentence; nothing in it a program or compiler can violate on its own.

cases.attempt: No program: a sub-queue is a division of a queue held by the message control system.
cases.reason: The definitional arm requires the defined thing to be a property OF THE USER'S PROGRAM; 'A logical hierarchical division of a queue' defines a structure of the MCS's queues, outside the program (the names had to add 'named in a program's communication description' to get there). The arm does not fit; the row needs another disposition (a Communication-module or environment arm), not this derivation.

cases.attempt: A program that violates 'the operand or reserved word immediately following the level indicator or level-number'.
cases.reason: The sentence names a position in a Data Division entry of the user's program; what may appear there is the level-number and clause formats' business; no program can be wrong against it.

cases.attempt: A CALL whose result depends on the callee being a 'called program'.
cases.reason: Two sentences: the first names the role of the CALL object in the run unit, the second makes the term a synonym; CALL's behaviour is the CALL rows'. No sentence a program or compiler can violate.

cases.attempt: probes\g-06-refute\tabconsec.cob: 01 W-T. 05 W-E PIC XX OCCURS 3. MOVE "AABBCC" TO W-T; W-E(1..3) must be AA/BB/CC, and MOVE "XY" TO W-E(2) makes W-T "AAXYCC".
cases.reason: 'A set of logically consecutive items of data that are defined in the Data Division of a COBOL program by means of the OCCURS clause' (§1985:III.2 p312, cite OK) states a property a program observes: the elements of a table follow one another in order within the group. A compiler that placed them out of order or apart changes the probe's outcome. 'logically consecutive' for tables occurs only in this definition in ANSI_COBOL_1985.md (grep), so no other row carries it. The witness runs correct at --std 85 (runs\tabconsec-001 TABCONSEC PASS); the row takes a test, not a derivation.

cases.attempt: A program whose outcome turns on an element being 'one of the repeated items comprising a table'.
cases.reason: One sentence naming the role; subscripting and OCCURS rows carry what a program sees; consecutiveness is p312's, not this row's.

cases.attempt: No program: a terminal is a device of the communication network.
cases.reason: 'The originator of a transmission to a queue, or the receiver of a transmission from a queue' defines an entity of the MCS environment; the reader's own compiler-at-1985 says 'a device of the message control system environment, outside any program'. The definitional arm requires a property of the user's program; it does not fit.

cases.attempt: COPY with a text-name that is not a user-defined word.
cases.reason: One sentence naming the COPY operand; formation of user-defined words and COPY resolution are other rows; nothing here is violable on its own.

cases.attempt: A CLOSE UNIT versus CLOSE REEL program.
cases.reason: 'A discrete portion of a storage medium, the dimensions of which are determined by each implementor' defines a property of the storage medium and the implementor, not of the user's program; the arm excludes a rule about the implementation. The synonym sentence's program-visible effect (UNIT = REEL in CLOSE) belongs to the CLOSE rows. The definitional arm does not fit as written.

cases.attempt: A file whose FD permits varying record sizes, writing and reading records of two lengths.
cases.reason: One sentence classifying records by what their FD/SD permits; which descriptions permit it and what READ/WRITE do are the RECORD clause and I-O rows; nothing in this sentence a compiler can violate.

cases.attempt: An item without OCCURS DEPENDING ON treated as variable occurrence; a program 'violating' the 'must'.
cases.reason: Both sentences read: the first names the term; the second ('Such an item must contain an OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause ... or be subordinate to such an item') fixes the term's membership; an item lacking ODO is simply not one, so no program can break it. ODO behaviour is the OCCURS rows'.

cases.attempt: A program using as a verb a word that expresses no action.
cases.reason: One sentence of vocabulary; statement formats decide which verbs exist; nothing violable.
